summary: A small dam and reservoir ten kilometres south of Ahwa — evening water views, and the ridge beside it doubles as the local sunset (and phone-signal) point.
description:
Temburgartha is Ahwa's water-and-sunset outing: a small irrigation dam south of town whose reservoir gives the forest country a rare open horizon. Locals drive out for the evening — the adjoining ridge is pinned on the map, with pleasing honesty, as 'Sunset point. Net point.': the spot where the view opens up and, just as usefully, where phone signal returns in a belt that mostly has none.

It is a picnic-and-pause place rather than a sight — banks, water, hills, chai from a flask — and it pairs with Kunda waterfall on the same side of town for Ahwa's easy half-day. The usual dam courtesies apply: viewpoints and banks are the visit, not the structure.

A village homestay, Vanvihar, sits a kilometre north — currently the only bed in this pocket of the district.
highlights: Open reservoir horizon in closed forest country
The local sunset point — and the belt's phone-signal spot
Pairs with Kunda falls for Ahwa's easy half-day

modes.road: South from Ahwa on the Temburgartha village road
modes.rail: Waghai (heritage narrow gauge); Bilimora Jn for broad gauge

access.last_mile: Short walks from the roadside to the banks and the sunset ridge

visit.notes: Respect any barriers near the dam structure — the banks and ridge are the visit.

seasonality.notes: Fullest just after the rains; low and hazy by late spring.

experience.photography_notes: Sunset over the water from the ridge; winter mornings bring waterbirds to the shallows.

warnings: No swimming — reservoir depths and slopes are treacherous
The ridge edge is unfenced; mind children at sunset

tips: Kunda falls in the afternoon, the dam ridge for sunset — Ahwa's easy double
Vanvihar stay home, a kilometre north, is the pocket's only homestay if you want to wake up here
The ridge is where your phone comes back to life — locals call it the net point for a reason

nearby.note: The picnic woods on the Wasurna side
